info.title: Business Events
info.description: Operations published by Extole Business Events components. Generated from the component contracts on my.extole.com.

post.description: Submits this business event from your backend as a person reaches it in the journey. Returns once identity resolution has completed, so the event is attributed to a known person.

event_id.description: Unique identifier for the submitted event.

person_id.description: Extole person the event resolved to.

Event tag (browser)
x-codeSamples.source:
<!-- On the page where the person reaches this step -->
<script type="text/javascript">
  /* Start Extole */
  (function(c,e,k,l,a){c[e]=c[e]||{};for(c[e].q=c[e].q||[];a<l.length;)k(l[a++],c[e])})(window,"extole",function(c,e){e[c]=e[c]||function(){e.q.push([c,arguments])}},["createZone"],0);
  /* End Extole */

  extole.createZone({
    name: 'template_tracked_business_event',
    data: {
      email: 'jane@example.com',
      partner_user_id: 'member-1042'
    }
  });
</script>

x-mint.content:
<Info>
**Two ways to send this event.** Send it from your backend with a client access token, as the **cURL** and **Node.js** examples show. Or fire it from the page with an event tag, as the **Event tag** example shows: the JavaScript SDK sends a zone request with the event name, and the platform records it as an event of the same name.
</Info>

<Warning>
Never put a client access token in a page. The event tag needs no token: the core tag identifies the person from the browser.
</Warning>

Replace `template_tracked_business_event` with the event name configured on your component, and pass the person's real email and your own ID for them.
